role.altitude: The actuary keeps deciding provisions, judging risks, setting negotiation positions, negotiating and testifying; searching old policy documents, assembling data packs, rerunning scenarios by hand, comparing quotes line by line and drafting memos and testimony from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted narratives against model output
Keeping the clause library and data packs current
role.ambitious_version: An actuary who can answer a reinsurer or a legislator with fresh figures the same week instead of next quarter.

tasks.short: Gather current provisions across products, determine policy contract provisions for each type of insurance, write them into the product specification and agree them with legal, underwriting and product management.

steps.what: Actuary gathers the current provisions and their versions across insurance products
Actuary determines policy contract provisions: cover, exclusions, options and guarantees for each type of insurance
Actuary writes the provisions into the product specification
Actuary agrees the provisions with legal, underwriting and product management

tasks.design: A clause library in the document system holds each standard provision with its versions and the products that use it, so the actuary finds the current wording without searching old policy documents. The product specification template pulls chosen clauses from the library, and the actuary edits product-specific text. Deciding provisions and agreeing them with legal, underwriting and product management stay with the actuary. Pricing the provisions belongs to the premium-rate task and is not priced here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provisions were scattered over policy documents of many product versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Clause libraries with versions and specification templates.
tasks.still_hard: New risks with no precedent wording.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing how a provision could be misused.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and retyping; deciding stays.

reach.learn: Whether standard clauses shorten legal review.

evidence.claim: Records apps with versions replace provisions kept in scattered documents.

assumptions: Boundary: deciding and specifying provisions; premium rates (task 24015) and explaining changes to customers (task 3513) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: legal keeps the clause library current with each released product version.
Deciding and agreeing keep their full time.
research_questions: Do wording inconsistencies between products fall?

incremental.description: Actuary tags new provisions for the clause library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new product lines with little standard wording; high: revisions of existing products.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather portfolio and market data, run risk models and scenarios, analyze results to provide expertise on managing risks and returns of investment or credit products, write the advice memo and discuss it with the institution.

steps.what: Actuary gathers portfolio, market and risk data
Actuary runs the risk models and scenarios
Actuary analyzes the results and forms the advice on managing risks and returns of investment products or credit offerings

loop.input: The scenario results and the actuary's key points.
loop.output: A draft memo with tables from the model output and a narrative of the movements.
loop.check: Every figure in the narrative must match the model output table; the actuary rewrites the advice section.
loop.stop: The actuary signs the memo, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative differs for each scenario set.

steps.what: Actuary discusses the advice with the institution

tasks.design: Portfolio and market data load on a schedule from the data platform into the model's input tables, instead of being copied into spreadsheets. Standard scenario sets run as saved configurations, and the actuary sets and checks the assumptions. A drafting step writes the memo's tables and movement narrative from the model output, with every figure tied to the output; the actuary writes the advice. Analysing results and discussing them with the institution stay with the actuary. No model scores individual borrowers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were copied by hand and scenarios rerun one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled data loads, saved scenario sets and drafting checked against output.
tasks.still_hard: Market regimes the models have not seen.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which risk matters most to this institution.

ambition.what: Refresh risk advice monthly instead of quarterly.

tasks.altitude: Less data handling and drafting; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether more frequent advice changes limits.

evidence.claim: Reserves and tables run in engines and code; a model can draft the movement narrative, checked against the figures.
Creditworthiness assessment of natural persons is a high-risk AI use; portfolio advice is not.

assumptions: Boundary: risk and return advice for products; pricing securities (task 3510) and explaining matters to executives (task 3504) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: the data platform team loads portfolio and market data on a schedule; about 80% of inputs come from there; s1 is priced at that share.
Analysis and discussion keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of inputs available on the data platform.
research_questions: Is advice delivered sooner after market moves?

incremental.description: Actuary keeps scenario sets and data mappings current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off analyses with new data; high: recurring advice at 80% scheduled data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the reinsurance submission, compare quotes and terms, decide the negotiation position, negotiate terms and conditions of reinsurance with other companies, and check the final wording against what was agreed.

steps.what: Actuary prepares the reinsurance submission: exposure data, claims history and current treaty terms
Actuary compares the reinsurers' quotes and terms

loop.input: The quotes and term sheets from reinsurers and brokers.
loop.output: A comparison table of limits, retentions, rates, exclusions and conditions, each with its page reference.
loop.check: Every figure must tie to its page; the actuary reads every exclusion and condition in full.
loop.stop: A quote whose figures do not tie is compared by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Quotes come in each reinsurer's own format.

steps.what: Actuary negotiates terms and conditions of reinsurance with reinsurers and brokers
Actuary checks the final treaty wording against the agreed terms

tasks.design: The submission pack is generated from the data platform in the market's usual format: exposure by band, loss triangles and current terms, instead of being assembled in spreadsheets for each renewal. Quotes are read into a comparison table with page references, and the actuary reads every exclusion and condition. Deciding the position, negotiating and checking the final wording stay with the actuary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Submissions were rebuilt in spreadsheets each renewal and quotes compared by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Data platforms with export templates and extraction checked against source pages.
tasks.still_hard: Reinsurers who change terms late in the round.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a reinsurer will accept.

reach.learn: Whether cleaner submissions bring better quotes.

evidence.claim: Extraction into fields works when totals and identifiers tie to the source, stopping on mismatch.
Insurers' AI documentation and monitoring were found short by the supervisor.

assumptions: Boundary: reinsurance renewal from submission to agreed wording; signing is management's.
Input contract for s1: exposure and claims data on the data platform, kept by the data team; about 80% of the pack comes from there; s1 is priced at that share.
Deciding, negotiating and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of treaties renewed each year.

already_counted.description: Actuary fixes comparison rows that do not tie to the quote.

incremental.description: Actuary keeps the submission template current with market formats.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few treaties with bespoke data; high: many treaties at 80% platform coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the proposed legislation, run impact calculations, write the testimony, prepare for questions and testify before public agencies on proposed legislation affecting businesses.

steps.what: Actuary reads the proposed legislation and marks the articles that affect the business

loop.input: The text of the proposal and the list of the company's product lines.
loop.output: A list of articles that touch the product lines, each quoted with a one-line note.
loop.check: Each item quotes its article; the actuary reads every listed article in full and skims the rest.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals are long and refer to other laws.

steps.what: Actuary runs impact calculations on the portfolio

loop.input: The actuary's key points, the impact figures and the quoted articles.
loop.output: A draft written testimony in the agency's format.
loop.check: Every figure must match the impact calculation; every legal reference must quote the article; the actuary rewrites the argument.
loop.stop: The actuary signs, or writes by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each testimony argues a different case.

steps.what: Actuary prepares for questions with colleagues and legal
Actuary testifies before public agencies and answers questions

tasks.design: A summarising step lists the articles of a proposal that touch the company's product lines, each quoted, so the actuary reads those in full first. Impact calculations reuse the existing reserving and pricing models with changed parameters instead of new spreadsheets. A drafting step writes a first testimony from the actuary's points, with each figure tied to the calculation and each legal reference quoted. Preparing for questions and testifying stay with the actuary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each proposal was read in full and its impact built in new spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Article lists with quotes, reusable models and drafting checked against figures.
tasks.still_hard: Hostile questions from members of the agency.
tasks.human_edge: Making a technical point land with legislators.
tasks.altitude: Less reading and drafting; testifying stays.

reach.learn: Whether the company responds earlier in consultations.

evidence.claim: A pharmaceutical company reports study reports drafted from approved text in minutes instead of weeks, with review cycles halved; vendor claim.
Staff who use AI systems need sufficient AI literacy.

assumptions: Boundary: testifying on proposed legislation; testifying in court (task 3507) is a sibling task.
Preparing and testifying keep their full time.
research_questions: Are impact figures ready earlier in the consultation?

incremental.description: Actuary keeps the product line list for the article search current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short proposals with simple impact; high: long proposals touching many product lines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
